title: Playing at the Ringside with Sharkey's band
summary: He describes the Sharkey band at the Ringside for Pete Herman, its members, and his role running it.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: For, listen, for is drum solos. I'm going to put it on a drum. That only came a few years back as drum solos. Then a drum player never did play a drum solo in my years. All he done was play drums and give that band the tempo. When that band hit one, two, that leader hit one, two, three, four, there he was. If it wasn't with the sticks, it was the brushes, but mostly the brushes. You understand? Because to tell you the truth, when you make a band and you want to hear the full harmony of the band and hear every instrument, the drums are supposed to be felt, not hoired. Because that's an instrument that can outdrown any other instrument. And when you start forcing those blowing instruments, then you ain't got nothing. Because then you're expanding the men and they can't play what they want to play. You see, myself, we played at the ringside with Sharky. And we had one, I'll tell you how good that band was. We had Charlie Cadela, Charlie Cadela, Harry Shields, Sharky, Joe Caparro. What's the boy, that drummer that Drowning himself? What do they call him again? Drowning himself? Yeah. Drummer? I don't remember any drummer.
Who's this band, the Sharky, the Chester? Yeah, but I mean did he play with Bersdorf too? No. That must have been before I came to town, Chief.

Oh yeah, yeah. What was his name? I can't think of it. Well anyway, from him we turned to Shaline. Then I doubled up on tuba and string bass. Freddie Newman was playing piano. Joe Caparro was playing guitar. Now, they gave me the business of being the man to run the band. They were the leader because I told them I didn't want anything about leadership. And up until today I don't. But I told them just what I would like for them to do and play. And I told the drummer, I says, fan brushes at all times. I says, and don't get wild, we want to feel it. And that's all. You see? Well we played at the ringside and we stood there for about four or five years at the ringside playing for Pete Hoyman. And.
